name: ecb-fx-rates
purpose: The euro foreign exchange reference rates the European Central Bank publishes each TARGET day: how many units of each currency one euro is worth at the daily fixing, as published, typed, and laid out one row per TARGET day and currency.
limitations: A reference fixing, not a market close or a tradable price, published at about 16:00 CET on each TARGET day. The 90-day file holds the last 90 days only, so history starts at the first file landed. A published rate that a later file changes fails the bronze audit (values_unchanged), which holds every later file until someone looks. The ECB's reference rates page says "The reference rates are published for information purposes only." and "Using the rates for transaction purposes is strongly discouraged.": do not price, settle or trade with them. The ECB accepts no liability for their use. Terms of reuse (the terms property and the licence link below, read by the owner on 2026-11-27): the rates may be used freely and passed on, provided they appear accurately, the ECB is cited as the source, and any change made to them is stated; a document sold with them in it tells its buyers the ECB's website gives them free of charge. How this product meets the last condition: bronze and silver_rates keep the published fixings unchanged (silver only types and keys them); gold_eur_rates_daily adds rows the ECB did not publish, a missing fixing carried forward for at most five TARGET days, each marked by is_carried and carried_days. Anyone passing gold on keeps those two columns and says the carried rows are not ECB fixings.
usage: Read fx_reference.ecb_fx_rates.gold_eur_rates_daily for one row per TARGET day and currency, a missing fixing carried from the last published one for at most five TARGET days (is_carried, carried_days); join on rate_available_at, not rate_date, to use a rate only once it was published. silver_rates holds the fixings exactly as published, one per day and currency.

links.description: The ECB's "Disclaimer & copyright" page, which states its terms of reuse; read by the owner on 2026-11-27 (the page shows no last-updated date). It allows free use of the information on condition that "it must appear accurately and the ECB must be cited as the source", and that a modification by the user "must be stated explicitly". Its one exception, documents that bear their authors' names, does not cover statistics.

outputs.purpose: One row per fixing date and currency of one landed 90-day file, the rate the string the ECB published. Each landed file adds its own rows, so a date appears once per file that holds it.

columns.name: rate_date
columns.description: The fixing's date (the file's Cube time), a TARGET day.

columns.name: currency
columns.description: The quoted currency's ISO 4217 code (USD); the base is always the euro.

columns.name: rate
columns.description: Units of the currency per one euro, the string exactly as published, such as 1.5000; typed in silver.

columns.name: source_file_sha256
columns.description: The landed file's sha256, set by the connector on every row (its lineage).

quality.name: no_future_date
quality.description: No fixing is dated after the fetch's day in UTC (domains/fx-reference/parsers/ecb_fx.py).

outputs.purpose: One row per TARGET day and currency, from the currency's first published fixing to the newest fixing of any currency: the day's rate, or the last published one carried for at most five TARGET days when the day has none, with when the rate could first be known.

columns.name: rate_date
columns.description: A TARGET day (reference-data.calendars.target_days, is_target_day); no weekend or TARGET holiday has a row.

columns.name: currency
columns.description: The quoted currency's ISO 4217 code; the base is always the euro.

columns.name: rate
columns.description: Units of the currency per one euro (quote units per euro), the ECB's reference fixing, not a market close. The day's own fixing, or when the day has none the last published one carried for up to five TARGET days; null once the last fixing is more than five TARGET days old.

columns.name: is_carried
columns.description: True when rate is an earlier day's fixing carried to this day (1 to 5 TARGET days); false on a published day and when rate is null.

columns.name: carried_days
columns.description: TARGET days since the currency's last published fixing: 0 on a published day, 1 to 5 while carried, 6 or more when rate is null. A weekend counts no days.

columns.name: rate_available_at
columns.description: When the rate could first be used, in UTC: 16:00 Frankfurt time (CET, or CEST in summer) on rate_date, the ECB's usual publication time. A convention, not the measured publication time; a carried rate counts from the day it is carried to, once that day's fixing failed to appear. Null when rate is null.

outputs.purpose: One row per fixing date and currency, the rate as an exact decimal: each fixing once, however many landed files repeat it, taken from the newest file that holds it.

columns.name: rate_date
columns.description: The fixing's date, a TARGET day. The partition source (year), so it is in the key: an incremental merge's unique key holds every partition source column.

columns.name: currency
columns.description: The quoted currency's ISO 4217 code; the base is always the euro.

columns.name: rate
columns.description: Units of the currency per one euro, the published string cast exactly to a decimal (1.5000 is 1.5); a reference fixing, not a market close.

columns.name: source_file_sha256
columns.description: The landed file the rate was taken from, the newest one holding this date and currency.

examples.description: The euro in US dollars on each TARGET day, with whether the rate was carried.
examples.sql: SELECT rate_date, rate, is_carried FROM fx_reference.ecb_fx_rates.gold_eur_rates_daily WHERE currency = 'USD' ORDER BY rate_date
